items.cheapest_check: Entra admin center -> Protection -> Conditional Access (the device-code policy's exclusions); Identity governance -> Privileged Identity Management -> Microsoft Entra roles -> Settings (activation notifications); External Identities -> External collaboration settings (guest invite restrictions).
items.unknown: Whether the five Entra SHOULD warnings are accepted risk or open work: managed devices for sign-in and for MFA registration (MS.AAD.3.7v1, MS.AAD.3.8v1), the device-code block and its exclusions (MS.AAD.3.9v1), activation alerts for five highly privileged roles (MS.AAD.7.9v1), and who may invite guests (MS.AAD.8.2v1).
items.why: A SHOULD shortfall needs a recorded decision, not just a result; the device-code exclusions decide whether Chain A has a second door, and managed-device policies need an Intune licence the run does not show.

items.cheapest_check: Microsoft Defender portal -> Email & collaboration -> Policies & rules -> Threat policies -> Email authentication settings -> DKIM.
items.unknown: Why DKIM is not enabled on tidewateradvisory.example (MS.EXO.3.1v1).
items.why: Unsigned mail from the default domain weakens DMARC alignment for that domain; turning DKIM on is cheap once the reason is known.

items.cheapest_check: Power BI admin portal -> Tenant settings: "Invite external users to your organization", "Block ResourceKey Authentication", "Interact with and share R and Python visuals".
items.unknown: Whether Power BI needs external-user invitations, ResourceKey authentication, and R and Python visuals (MS.POWERBI.3.1v1, MS.POWERBI.5.1v1, MS.POWERBI.6.1v1).
items.why: Each is allowed by the baseline only where a mission need is stated; the run cannot see the need, only the setting.

items.cheapest_check: Power Platform admin center -> Environments (purpose and owner), then Policies -> Data policies.
items.unknown: What the non-default Power Platform environment is for, and whether it needs its own DLP policy (MS.POWERPLATFORM.2.2v1).
items.why: The default-environment fix (F-13) does not cover it; a second environment with no DLP policy keeps Chain D open there.

items.cheapest_check: Defender portal -> Threat policies -> Safe Attachments -> Global settings; Anti-phishing -> the policy's impersonation lists; Microsoft Purview -> Data loss prevention -> Policies -> locations.
items.unknown: The four Security Suite warnings: Safe Attachments for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams (MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.4v1), impersonation protection for sensitive users and partner domains (MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.1v1, MS.SECURITYSUITE.2.3v1), and DLP locations beyond Devices (MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.2v1).
items.why: Two of them read as warnings only because the run configuration lists no sensitive users or partner domains (H2), so the human look decides whether they are gaps; 1.4 and 3.2 bear on Chains C and D.
